Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

covr (development version)

  • to_sonarqube() now writes file paths relative to the package root (e.g. R/foo.R) instead of prefixing them with the package name, so the report works when the package is the root of the SonarQube project. Use the new path_prefix argument if the package is in a subdirectory of the project, e.g. path_prefix = "mypkg" restores the previous paths (#636).

  • package_coverage() now accepts outDir in ... to save the test and example output to a directory of your choice, instead of failing with “formal argument”outDir” matched by multiple actual arguments” (#518).

  • package_coverage(allow_failures = TRUE) now also keeps install_path when failures are reported as warnings, so the output files they refer to can be inspected (#554).

  • file_coverage(), code_coverage(), environment_coverage(), function_coverage() and with_coverage() now include code run in processes forked by parallel’s mclapply(), mcparallel() and related functions, as package_coverage() already did. Set options(covr.fix_parallel_mcexit = FALSE) to turn this off (#410).

  • package_coverage() now warns when an R process started by the tests, such as a Shiny app, callr session or future worker, loaded the package but did not save its coverage because it was killed or was still running when the tests finished. That coverage used to be silently missing, so the results could vary from run to run (#438).

  • Lines excluded with # nocov are no longer reported as uncovered when they are part of a larger expression that is not entirely excluded, such as the first and last lines of a function defined inside another function (#594).

  • codecov() now throws an error if the upload to codecov.io fails, so CI jobs that upload coverage fail instead of silently succeeding. Rate limits (HTTP 429) and Codecov outages (HTTP 5xx) give a warning instead, so they don’t fail CI (#565).

  • New to_lcov() writes coverage as an LCOV tracefile (lcov.info), for genhtml and other tools that read the LCOV format (#442, thanks to @MichaelChirico for the initial implementation in #637).

  • New to_lcov() writes coverage as an LCOV tracefile (lcov.info), for genhtml and other tools that read the LCOV format (#442, thanks to @MichaelChirico for the initial implementation in #637).

  • package_coverage() no longer reports 0% coverage for packages whose last file in R/ is empty (#522).

  • New coverage_to_markdown() formats coverage as a markdown table, optionally compared against a baseline, for GitHub Actions job summaries or pull request comments (#519).

  • New coverage_to_markdown() formats coverage as a markdown table, optionally compared against a baseline, for GitHub Actions job summaries or pull request comments (#519).

  • Functions nested inside lists and environments, such as fns <- list(a = function(x) x), functions defined inside local() and ggproto methods, can now be traced. This is off by default; enable it for a package with Config/covr/full_traversal: true in its DESCRIPTION, or with options(covr.full_traversal = TRUE) (#113).

  • New with_coverage() measures the coverage of arbitrary code, such as testthat::test_file(), run against an environment like a package namespace loaded with pkgload::load_all(). This allows tools such as devtools::test_coverage_active_file() to use testthat’s own runner instead of recreating it, so setup files and fixtures found with testthat::test_path() work as they do in testthat::test_file() (related to #543, #551).

  • tally_coverage() gains by = "function", with one row for each function, so zero_coverage(cov, by = "function") lists the functions that were never run. percent_coverage() and print() also accept it (#245).

  • report() now bundles Bootstrap 3.4.1 instead of 3.3.5, which had known security vulnerabilities (#639).

  • value() now works on coverage objects of R code; it previously errored for anything but compiled code. The structure of coverage objects is now documented in ?coverage, and as.data.frame() on a coverage object in ?as.data.frame.coverage (#564).

  • report() now keeps the Files / Source tabs at the top of the page while scrolling, and returning to the file list restores its scroll position (#232).

  • Fix “argument is missing, with no default” errors when tracing a switch() call with fall-through cases (a = ,) whose subject is piped in with the base pipe (x |> switch(...)) (#630).

  • Lines of compiled code that gcov reports as only partially executed (e.g. if (x) f(); when f() never runs) are no longer dropped from the coverage. They count as covered, or as not covered with options(covr.gcov_partial = "uncovered") (#604). covr now runs gcov with -a so partial lines are also found with llvm-cov, the gcov on macOS, and older versions of gcc (#610).

  • covr_error conditions (and the covr_warnings from allow_failures) now keep the whole failure output in $output and its file in $file. The message shows the last 50 lines and is bounded by warning.length measured in characters (it was measured inconsistently in bytes, so multibyte output could leave the message empty), and print() shows the last n lines, 50 by default. The number of lines can be set with options(covr.failure_lines) (#570, #642).

  • The RStudio addin now prints a message when it starts calculating coverage, so there is feedback before the report opens (#404).

  • Fix a warning, and possibly an error under options(warn = 2), when tracing a switch() call with a trailing comma (#483).

  • Trace files are now written atomically, and a failure to save or read one is reported as a covr_error (a covr_warning with allow_failures = TRUE) naming the file, rather than a cryptic readRDS() error (#509).

  • package_coverage() now only deletes install_path if coverage succeeds, so the test output referenced in failure messages can be inspected (@hadley, #615).

  • Avoid cyclic namespace dependency when running coverage on httr and its dependencies, such as R6 (#623).

  • package_coverage() gains an allow_failures argument (default getOption("covr.allow_failures", FALSE)). When TRUE, failing tests, vignettes, examples or code produce a warning instead of an error and coverage is still returned, e.g. so covr::report() can be viewed after a long test run with a failure (#533).

  • Coverage is now reported for S7 property getters, setters, and validators with S7 > 0.2.2, which stores class callbacks in a shared class reference (@t-kalinowski, #646).

  • Fix a generational garbage-collection bug when replacing traced functions in place, without permanently retaining their bodies or environments (#640).

  • Tracing a package is faster, as parse data now keeps text only for terminal tokens (@erkurtharun, #644).

  • merge_coverage() is much faster for packages with many traces (@erkurtharun, #643).

  • With options(covr.record_tests = TRUE), merging coverage now correctly renumbers the test indices of traces that are absent from the first coverage object (#643).

  • Fix compilation of the TestCompiled test package on R 4.6 by using public REAL() and INTEGER() accessors instead of the non-API DATAPTR().

  • Fix a rare edge case where count_test was called before .current_test has been initialized leading to crash (@maksymiuks, #631).

  • Fix rare error in clean_coverage_tests where NA were being compared in if condition (@maksymiuks, #631).

  • clean_coverage_tests now uses length(x) == 0 instead of is.null(x) to account for NULL values and integer(0) at the same time (@maksymiuks, #631).

covr 3.6.5

CRAN release: 2025-11-09

New Features and improvements

  • Added support for klmr/box modules. This works best with file_coverage(). (@radbasa, #491)

  • Performance improvement for compiled code with a lot of compilation units (@krlmlr, #611)

  • Fix R CMD check NOTE for upcoming R 4.6: non-API calls to SET_BODY, SET_CLOENV, SET_FORMALS (@t-kalinowski, #587)

Fixes and minor improvements

  • Messages are now displayed using cli instead of crayon (@olivroy, #591).

  • covr now uses testthat::with_mocked_bindings() for its internal testing (@olivroy, #595).

  • Fix a bug preventing package_coverage() from running tests when install_path is set to a relative path (@gergness, #517, #548).

  • Fixed a performance regression and an error triggered by a change in R 4.4.0. (@kyleam, #588)

  • Fixed an issue where attempting to generate code coverage on an already-loaded package could fail on Windows. (@kevinushey, #574)

  • Prevent covr.record_tests option from logging duplicate tests when the same line of testing code is hit repeatedly, as in a loop. (@dgkf, #528)

  • Normalize install_path path before creating directory to prevent failures when running covr in a subprocess using a path with Windows \\ path separators. (@maksymiuks, #592)

covr 3.6.4

CRAN release: 2023-11-09

  • Fix for a failing test on CRAN

covr 3.6.3

CRAN release: 2023-10-10

  • Updates to internal usage of is.atomic() to work with upcoming R release (@mmaechler , #542)

  • package_coverage() now works correctly with ignore files when it is not run in the package root directory (@mpadge, #538)

covr 3.6.2

CRAN release: 2023-03-25

  • Fix S3 generic/method signature consistency and skip an R6 test on R-devel, for CRAN checks (#534).

covr 3.6.1

CRAN release: 2022-08-26

  • to_cobertura() is now explicit about the doctype of the resulting XML. It also sets a source path if recorded. (@mmyrte, #524)

  • The internal generic merge_coverage() now correctly registers the S3 methods.

  • The internal test for recording large calls no longer assumes R is on the system PATH.

covr 3.6.0

CRAN release: 2022-08-24

  • Added covr.record_tests option. When TRUE, this enables the recording of the trace of the tests being executed and adds an itemization of which tests result in the execution of each trace. For more details see ?covr.record_tests (@dgkf, #463, #485, #503)

  • as.data.frame() now returns an 0 row data frame when there are no functions in a package (#427)

  • codecov() is now more robust when coverage is not the output from package_coverage() and token is not provided (#456)

  • package_coverage(code = ) now accepts character vectors of length greater than 1 (@bastistician, #481)

  • package_coverage() now handles packages with install or render time examples (#488)

  • package_coverage() now sets the environment variable R_TESTS to the tests-startup.R file like R CMD check does (#420)

  • report() now provides a more detailed error message if the DT and htmltools dependencies are not installed (#500).

  • Fix parse_gcov bug when package is stored in directory with regex special characters, see #459

  • Error/warning thrown for, respectively, missing gcov or empty parsed gcov output (@stephematician, #448)

  • Support Google Cloud Build uploading reports to Codecov.io (@MarkEdmondson1234 #469)

  • covr is now licensed as MIT (#454)

covr 3.5.1

CRAN release: 2020-09-16

  • Generated files from cpp11 are now ignored (#437)

  • codecov() and coveralls() now retry failed requests before raising an error (#428, @jameslamb)

covr 3.5.0

CRAN release: 2020-03-06

  • codecov() now supports GitHub Actions for public repositories without having to specify a token.

  • New to_sonarqube() function added to support SonarQube generic XML format (@nibant, @Delfic, #413).

covr 3.4.0

CRAN release: 2019-11-26

  • codecov() now supports GitHub Actions.

  • New in_covr() function added to return true if code is being run by covr (#407).

  • file_coverage(), environment_coverage() and function_coverage() now set R_COVR=true, to be consistent with package_coverage() (#407)

covr 3.3.2

CRAN release: 2019-10-16

  • Fix test failures in the development version of R (4.0.0) (#400)

covr 3.3.1

CRAN release: 2019-08-23

  • Fix inadvertent regression in return visibility when functions are covered. covr versions prior to 3.3.0 surrounded each statement in { blocks. covr 3.3.0 switched to using ({, but this caused an inadvertent regression, as ( will make the result visible it is the last expression in a function. Using if (TRUE) { restores the previous behavior. (#391, #392)

covr 3.3.0

CRAN release: 2019-08-06

New Features

  • New azure() function added to make it easy to use covr on Azure Pipelines (#370)

  • Work around issues related to the new curly curly syntax in rlang (#379, #377, rlang#813)

  • Compiled code coverage has been improved, in particular C++ templates now contain the merged coverage of all template instances, even if the instances were defined in separate compilation units. (#390)

Bugfixes and minor improvements

  • codecov() now includes support for the flags field (#365)

  • codecov now looks codecov.yml for token if CODECOV_TOKEN envvar is not set (@MishaCivey #349).

  • per_line() now does not track lines with only punctuation such as } or { (#387)

  • tally_coverage() now includes compiled code, like it did previously (#384)

  • Define the necessary coverage flags for C++14, C++17 and C++20 (#369).

  • to_cobertura() now works with Cobertura coverage-04.dtd (@samssann, #337).

  • R6 class generators prefixed with . are now included in coverage results (@jameslamb, #356).

  • package_coverage() gains option pre_clean, set to FALSE to disable cleaning of existing objects before running package_coverage() (@jpritikin, #375)
